cases.name: Gabrielle Chloe' "Gabbiee" Swainson
cases.about: Gabbiee was an honors student at Ridge View High School. She was just days away from beginning her sophomore year when she disappeared. Her obituary said, "Although Gabbiee's life expired at a young age, she lived a full life through her love for the arts. It became her peace and comfort. It became her joy and laughter. It was her strength and courage. She expressed herself through singing, dancing, drawing, writing letters and fictional stories, texting with her friends and more recently returning to her passion of playing the guitar. All of these extracurricular and leisure activities were performed in excellence while she continued to maintain her honor roll status. Although Gabbiee was already involved in several activities, her ambitious spirit led her to try out for the Ridgeview High School cheerleading squad. With persistence, she became a member of the squad for her upcoming sophomore year. Gabbiee was a member of the LM Atkinson South Carolina Federated Club. She performed with Columbia City Jazz and participated in many competitions. She took classes at Southeastern Ballet and performed at the Columbia International Festival. She danced with Hathalah Meihadash dance group at age five (5) and danced at her church, Right Direction Church International. She took gymnastics classes early on at All Star Gymnastics and later with Flip City and Carolina Crossfire Cheer. She began guitar and voice lessons at Dent Middle, where she was also chosen to be a member of the Tri-M Music Honor Society. She continued to develop her musical talent at GMG Music Studio and took private guitar lessons at Star Music Company. Additionally, Gabbiee modeled with Shaw's Model and Talent Center at age five (5) and returned to it with DeAbreu Modeling Agency. Although we will miss her every day, especially her beautiful eyes, beautiful smile and sense of style, she will forever remain in our hearts. Our immediate family is proud of Gabrielle's achievements and we are privileged to have created wonderful memories to hold onto throughout the minutes, days and years to come."
cases.narrative:
He went into Swainson's house with a key he'd stolen, forced her out of the home, took the teenager to his house in Elgin, tied her up, suffocated her, and then buried her.

A year later, Grant eventually led officials to her grave in a wooded area in Elgin, not far from where Laster was found.

cases.name: Jessie Foster Brown
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Jessie received her formal education in the Clarksdale Private School system, and graduated from Immaculate Conception Catholic School in Clarksdale, Mississippi, in 1960. In 1961, Jessie relocated to New York where she met the love of her life, Melvin Brown Sr. Jessie was united in matrimony to the late Melvin Brown, Sr. on January 27, 1973, in Great Neck, New York. Jessie and Melvin, later in 1975 relocated to Columbia, SC to join their blended family as one. The union blessed them to have seven children: three daughters and four sons. 

On, October 3, 1982, Jessie was baptized in the name of Jesus Christ and received the Holy Ghost, according to Acts 2:38 and Acts 2:4 at the Progressive Church of Our Lord Jesus Christ for over 40 years. Jessie was a dedicated faithful member serving on baptism, hospitality, volunteer -flower bearers and usher committees until her passing. 

Jessie love for children lead her in January of 1984 to become a Richland School District One substitute teacher for Hyatt Park Elementary School. By Sept of 1984 Jessie was hired as a full-time Instructional Assistant for 4k and Kindergarten. Jessie love for teaching spand over 19 years until her retirement in 2003. She had a special love for children and that love lead her to expand her years of service to Fantasy Island Child Care Center for over 30 years. Jessie lived by “Be steadfast and immovable always abounding in good work” Mosiah 5:15, “That when you do something, give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain” 1 Corinthians 15:58."

"Ms. Brown was the type of person that you couldn't help but to get close to," said Columbia Fire Chief Aubrey Jenkins. "She was always willing to help. It didn't matter who it was, where it was, she was always willing to help."

Chief Jenkins said he went to church with Ms. Brown. He described her as thoughtful, caring, and he thought of her as family.

"She was a great mother figure to me because she was just that type of person. She was just humbled and spirited," Jenkins said.

Jessie Brown worked at Fantasy Island Daycare for more than 30 years—serving as one of the longest working staff members. 

The owner of the daycare, Ron Scott, said Ms. Brown touched everyone she met and was always loving and positive. 

"I used to tease her and call her, at her age of 80 plus, the energizer bunny, because at 80+ she never walked with any type of walking stick or any assistance," Scott said. "She would be out in the playground running with the kids like someone 20 or 30 years younger."

cases.name: Sha’Neal Amel Brown
cases.about:
ShaNeal was a student at Eau Claire High School and was set to graduate in May. A family friend said she was driven and had high goals. 

Her grandmother, Jessie Brown worked at Fantasy Island Daycare for more than 30 years—serving as one of the longest working staff members. 

"She definitely was 100% behind ShaNeal and making sure that she had everything she needed to graduate and go beyond high school and college," said family friend Dominic Sims. "She always made sure she was taken care of. They were like two peas in a pod. So, if you see one, you would see the other. So they definitely were very, very close, and you could tell that, and you could tell that they really cared for one another."
